paragraphs: A tool library lends drills, ladders and saws to residents for a small annual fee, on the principle that most people use a given tool only a few hours a year. Proponents emphasize the savings: a household that borrows a power washer twice a year avoids a purchase of several hundred dollars. The less obvious benefit may be social. Borrowers must return in person, and a visit often turns into a conversation with a volunteer who can advise on the job, or with another borrower facing a similar repair. Over time such encounters appear to knit together neighbors who might otherwise never meet, an effect that no hardware store, whatever its prices, is likely to match.
